course.title: Cake Baking and Decorating
course.tagline: Bake moist cakes and decorate them beautifully for birthdays and weddings.

days.title: Cake Baking Basics
days.goal: Know your tools, ingredients, and how a cake rises.

video.title: How to Cover a Cake in Fondant

steps: Find your tools: cake tins, a whisk, a spatula, and baking paper.
Learn the main ingredients: flour, sugar, butter, eggs, and baking powder.
Baking powder is a powder that makes gas when heated, so cakes rise.
Line your tin with baking paper so the cake comes out clean.
Preheat the oven. A cake needs steady heat from the start.
days.task: Line a cake tin with baking paper and check your oven heat.
days.challenge: Measure all your ingredients for tomorrow's sponge cake today.

options: Baking powder or beaten eggs make gas that lifts the cake
quiz.explain: Baking powder and beaten eggs make gas. The gas lifts the cake as it bakes.

quiz.q: Why line a cake tin with paper?
options: So the cake comes out clean without sticking
quiz.explain: Paper stops the cake sticking to the tin.

quiz.q: Why preheat the oven for cakes?
options: Cakes need steady heat from the start to rise well
quiz.explain: A cold oven gives a flat, heavy cake.

days.title: Your First Vanilla Sponge Cake
days.goal: Bake a soft vanilla sponge cake.

video.title: How to Make Chocolate Ganache

steps: Cream means beat butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each one.
Add vanilla and a little milk.
Fold in the flour gently with a spatula. Do not stir hard.
Bake at 180°C for 25 to 30 minutes. Test with a toothpick.
days.task: Bake a vanilla sponge cake.
days.challenge: Cut the cake in half and fill it with jam.

quiz.q: What does 'cream butter and sugar' mean?
options: Beat them together until pale and fluffy
quiz.explain: Creaming beats air into the butter and sugar, which makes the cake light.

quiz.q: Why add eggs one at a time?
options: So the mix does not split
quiz.explain: Adding eggs slowly keeps the mix smooth. All at once can make it split.

options: Hard stirring pushes the air out and makes a heavy cake
quiz.explain: Folding keeps the air in. Stirring hard pushes it out.

days.title: Chocolate Cake in 15 Minutes
days.goal: Bake a quick, moist chocolate cake.

video.title: How to Make a Vanilla Buttercream Recipe

steps: Mix flour, cocoa, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl.
Add eggs, milk, and oil. Mix until smooth.
Pour into a lined tin.
Bake at 180°C until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
days.task: Bake a chocolate cake.
days.challenge: Make a second one with a little coffee in the mix and compare the taste.

quiz.q: What does cocoa add to a cake?
quiz.explain: Cocoa gives chocolate flavour and colour.

quiz.q: Why cool a cake in the tin for 10 minutes?
options: It firms up so it does not break when you turn it out
quiz.explain: A hot cake is soft and breaks easily. Ten minutes firms it up.

quiz.q: How do you test if a cake is done?
quiz.explain: A clean toothpick means the middle is cooked.

days.title: Cupcakes: Small Cakes, Big Fun
days.goal: Bake vanilla cupcakes.

video.title: How to Make a Vanilla Sponge Cake Recipe

steps: Line a cupcake tray with paper cases.
Make a sponge mix, the same as a cake.
Fill each case two-thirds full. No more, or they will spill over.
Bake at 180°C for 18 to 20 minutes.
Cool fully before adding any topping.
days.task: Bake 12 vanilla cupcakes.
days.challenge: Make half chocolate and half vanilla in the same tray.

quiz.q: How full should a cupcake case be?
quiz.explain: Two-thirds full leaves room for the cake to rise without spilling.

quiz.q: Why cool cupcakes fully before topping?
quiz.explain: Topping on a warm cupcake melts and slides off.
Cupcakes are small, so they bake in 18 to 20 minutes.

days.title: Buttercream: The Classic Frosting
days.goal: Make smooth vanilla buttercream.

video.title: Vanilla Cupcake Recipe

steps: Buttercream is soft butter beaten with icing sugar.
Beat the butter first until it is pale and soft.
Add icing sugar a little at a time.
Add a spoon of milk and vanilla. Beat until smooth and fluffy.
Taste it. Add more sugar if you want it sweeter.
days.task: Make a bowl of vanilla buttercream.
days.challenge: Make a chocolate version by adding cocoa.

options: Soft butter beaten with icing sugar
quiz.explain: Buttercream is butter and icing sugar beaten together.

quiz.q: Why add icing sugar a little at a time?
options: So it mixes in smoothly without a cloud of sugar
quiz.explain: Adding sugar slowly stops it flying everywhere and keeps the mix smooth.

quiz.q: What does milk do in buttercream?
options: It makes it soft and easy to spread
quiz.explain: A little milk softens buttercream so it spreads well.

days.title: Frosting a Cake Smoothly
days.goal: Frost a cake so it looks smooth and neat.

video.title: How to Pipe a Cupcake

steps: Let the cake cool fully. Warm cake melts frosting.
Cut off the domed top so the cake is flat.
Put a little frosting on the plate so the cake does not move.
Spread a thin first coat. This is the crumb coat. It traps the crumbs.
Chill for 20 minutes, then add the final thick coat and smooth it.
days.task: Frost your sponge cake with buttercream.
days.challenge: Try smoothing with a hot knife dipped in warm water.

options: A thin first coat that traps crumbs
quiz.explain: A thin first coat traps loose crumbs so the final coat stays clean.

quiz.q: Why chill the cake after the crumb coat?
options: So the crumb coat sets firm before the final coat
quiz.explain: A firm crumb coat stops crumbs mixing into the final layer.

quiz.q: Why cut off the domed top?
options: A flat top stacks and frosts neatly
quiz.explain: A flat cake is easy to stack and frost smoothly.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Frosted Celebration Cake
days.goal: Bake and frost a full celebration cake.

video.title: How to Create a Drip Cake

steps: Bake two sponge layers.
Make buttercream while the cakes cool.
Level both layers so they are flat.
Stack with buttercream in the middle, then crumb coat and chill.
Add the final coat, smooth it, and decorate simply.
days.task: Bake and frost a celebration cake for your household.
days.challenge: Write 'Happy Day' on the cake with a piping bag or a toothpick.

options: Two layers make a taller, more special cake
quiz.explain: Two layers stacked make a proper celebration cake.
Buttercream or jam between layers adds flavour and holds them together.

quiz.q: Why is a crumb coat important?
options: It traps crumbs so the final coat is clean
quiz.explain: The crumb coat locks crumbs away so the final coat looks smooth.

project.title: Bake and Frost a Celebration Cake
project.brief: Bake two sponge layers, fill, frost, and decorate a celebration cake.
checks: Two sponge layers baked and cooled

days.title: Piping Basics: Stars and Swirls
days.goal: Pipe buttercream stars and swirls with a piping bag.

video.title: How to Create a Gumpaste Bow

steps: Fit a star nozzle into a piping bag.
Fill the bag half full. Twist the top closed.
Hold the bag straight down. Squeeze, then lift.
Practise on a plate first: stars, swirls, and shells.
Pipe a border around the edge of a cake.
days.task: Pipe a border around a cake or cupcakes.
days.challenge: Pipe 12 cupcakes with a swirl on top.

quiz.q: How full should a piping bag be?
quiz.explain: Half full gives you control. A full bag is hard to squeeze.

quiz.q: What does a star nozzle make?
quiz.explain: A star nozzle makes a ridged star shape.

quiz.q: Why practise on a plate first?
options: So your hand learns the pressure before the real cake
quiz.explain: Practice on a plate builds control before you touch the cake.

days.title: Chocolate Ganache: Rich and Glossy
days.goal: Make chocolate ganache for drips and coating.

video.title: The 1m vs 2D Piping Nozzle

steps: Ganache is chocolate mixed with hot cream.
Chop chocolate small so it melts fast.
Heat cream until just steaming. Do not boil it.
Pour the cream over the chocolate. Wait 2 minutes, then stir.
Stir from the middle out until it is smooth and shiny.
days.task: Make a bowl of chocolate ganache.
days.challenge: Pour it over a cake and let it drip down the sides.

quiz.explain: Ganache is chocolate and hot cream stirred together.

options: So the heat melts the chocolate first
quiz.explain: Waiting lets the hot cream melt the chocolate before you stir.

quiz.q: Why stir from the middle out?
options: It keeps the ganache smooth and shiny
quiz.explain: Stirring from the middle keeps air out and the ganache glossy.

days.title: Drip Cakes: The Modern Look
days.goal: Make a drip cake with ganache.

video.title: Two Tone Buttercream Rose Cupcake Tutorial

steps: Bake and frost a cake smoothly. Chill it until the frosting is firm.
Make ganache and let it cool until it is thick but still runny.
Spoon ganache on the top edge and let it drip down.
Fill in the top with more ganache.
Add sweets, fruit, or sprinkles on top.
days.task: Make a drip cake.
days.challenge: Try a white chocolate drip on a chocolate cake.

quiz.q: Why chill the frosted cake first?
options: Firm frosting holds the drip in place
quiz.explain: Cold, firm frosting stops the drip running too far.

quiz.q: How thick should drip ganache be?
quiz.explain: Thick but runny ganache drips slowly and stops where you want.

quiz.q: What can you put on top of a drip cake?
quiz.explain: Sweets, fruit, and sprinkles finish a drip cake.

days.title: Fondant: Covering a Cake
days.goal: Cover a cake in fondant, the smooth sugar icing.

video.title: Chocolate Cake in 15 Minutes! Soft, Delicious & Easy!

steps: Fondant is a soft sugar dough you roll out like pastry.
Frost the cake with buttercream first. This is the glue.
Knead the fondant until soft. Roll it out on a surface dusted with icing sugar.
Lift it over the cake and smooth it down from the top.
Trim the extra at the bottom with a knife.
days.task: Cover a small cake in fondant.
days.challenge: Practise rolling fondant and cutting shapes from it.

options: A soft sugar dough rolled over cakes
quiz.explain: Fondant is a sugar dough that gives cakes a smooth, clean finish.

options: It acts as glue for the fondant
quiz.explain: Buttercream under fondant holds it in place.

quiz.q: Why dust the surface with icing sugar?
options: So the fondant does not stick
quiz.explain: Icing sugar stops fondant sticking to the table.

days.title: Piping Nozzles: 1M and 2D
days.goal: Learn the two most useful piping nozzles.

video.title: How To Frost A Cake With Smooth Buttercream

steps: The 1M nozzle makes big swirls and rosettes.
The 2D nozzle makes smaller, tighter flowers.
Practise both on a plate: swirls, rosettes, and stars.
Use the 1M for cupcake tops and the 2D for small flowers.
Keep your hand steady and squeeze with even pressure.
days.task: Pipe rosettes with the 1M nozzle on 6 cupcakes.
days.challenge: Pipe small flowers with the 2D nozzle on a cake.

quiz.explain: The 1M makes big, open swirls and rosettes.
The 2D makes smaller, more detailed flowers.
Uneven pressure gives uneven, messy shapes.

days.title: Cupcake Piping: Roses and Two Tones
days.goal: Pipe roses and two-tone cupcakes.

video.title: Your Guide to Frosting a Cake with Smooth Buttercream

steps: Two-tone means two colours of frosting in one bag.
Put each colour on one side of the bag.
Pipe a rose: start in the middle and circle out.
Practise roses on a plate until they look neat.
Pipe roses on cupcakes for a party box.
days.task: Pipe buttercream roses on 6 cupcakes.
days.challenge: Make a two-tone swirl on 6 more cupcakes.

options: Two colours of frosting piped together
quiz.explain: Two-tone means two colours in one bag, piped at the same time.

quiz.q: How do you pipe a buttercream rose?
options: Start in the middle and circle out
quiz.explain: A rose starts in the middle and circles outward.

quiz.q: Why practise roses on a plate?
options: So you learn the shape before the real cupcakes
quiz.explain: Practice builds skill without spoiling the real cupcakes.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Decorated Cupcake Box
days.goal: Bake and decorate a box of 12 cupcakes.

video.title: Frost a Cake with Smooth Buttercream

steps: Bake 12 cupcakes: 6 vanilla, 6 chocolate.
Make buttercream in two colours.
Pipe 6 with swirls and 6 with roses.
Add sprinkles and a simple topper to each one.
Pack them in a box and share them.
days.task: Make a decorated box of 12 cupcakes.
days.challenge: Price the box as if you were selling it.

quiz.explain: Two flavours give people a choice and show your range.

options: Neat piping, even sizes, and tidy decoration
quiz.explain: Neat piping and even sizes make cupcakes look professional.

options: It teaches you the real cost of your work
quiz.explain: Pricing turns decorating into a business skill.

project.title: Make a Decorated Cupcake Box
project.brief: Bake 12 cupcakes in two flavours and decorate them with piping.

days.title: Semi-Naked Cakes: The Rustic Look
days.goal: Make a semi-naked cake, where the sponge shows through.

video.title: How To Frost A Flawless Semi-Naked Cake

steps: A semi-naked cake has only a thin coat of frosting.
Bake two or three layers and level them.
Stack with buttercream between the layers.
Spread a thin coat on the sides. Let some sponge show.
Top with fresh fruit or flowers.
days.task: Make a semi-naked cake.
days.challenge: Top it with fresh fruit and serve it at a meal.

options: A cake with a thin coat so the sponge shows through
quiz.explain: Semi-naked means a thin coat of frosting with sponge showing through.

quiz.q: Why is a semi-naked cake good for beginners?
options: You do not need a perfect smooth coat
quiz.explain: A thin coat hides small mistakes and still looks good.

quiz.q: What can you top a semi-naked cake with?
quiz.explain: Fresh fruit or flowers suit the rustic look.

days.title: Gumpaste Bows and Sugar Flowers
days.goal: Make a gumpaste bow for a cake topper.

video.title: How to Cover a Cake in Fondant

steps: Gumpaste is a sugar dough that dries hard.
Roll it thin and cut strips.
Fold strips into loops for a bow. Let them dry overnight.
Glue the loops together with a little water or icing.
Place the bow on top of a cake.
days.task: Make a gumpaste bow.
days.challenge: Make simple sugar flowers with a cutter and let them dry.

options: A sugar dough that dries hard
quiz.explain: Gumpaste dries hard, so it is good for bows and flowers.

options: So it sets hard and holds its shape
quiz.explain: Dry gumpaste is strong and keeps its shape on a cake.
A drop of water or icing acts as glue for sugar pieces.

days.title: Cake Toppers and Simple Decorations
days.goal: Decorate cakes with toppers, fruit, and chocolate.

video.title: How to Make Chocolate Ganache

steps: Use fresh fruit, chocolate pieces, or a simple topper.
Place big items first, then fill gaps with small ones.
Keep the design simple. Less is often more.
Use a clean, dry cake board under the cake.
Take a photo in good light before serving.
days.task: Decorate a cake with fruit and chocolate pieces.
days.challenge: Make a cake topper from paper or card for a birthday.

options: Big items set the design, small ones fill the gaps
quiz.explain: Big pieces first, then small ones fill the gaps.
A simple design looks clean and professional.

quiz.q: Why take a photo in good light?
options: Good light shows the true colours
quiz.explain: Good light makes your cake look its best in photos.

days.title: Wedding Cakes: The Basics
days.goal: Plan a simple two-tier wedding cake.

video.title: How to Make a Vanilla Buttercream Recipe

steps: A tier is one cake stacked on another.
Bake two sizes: a big bottom tier and a smaller top tier.
Use dowels (sticks) inside the bottom tier to hold the top one.
Frost both tiers smoothly and stack them carefully.
Decorate with white frosting and simple flowers.
days.task: Plan a two-tier cake on paper: sizes, flavours, and colours.
days.challenge: Bake a small two-tier cake for practice.

quiz.explain: A tier is one layer of a stacked cake.

options: Sticks inside the cake that hold the top tier up
quiz.explain: Dowels stop the top tier sinking into the bottom one.

quiz.q: Why plan a wedding cake on paper first?
options: So you know sizes, flavours, and costs before baking
quiz.explain: Planning on paper stops mistakes on a cake that matters.

days.title: Costing Cakes: Price Your Work
days.goal: Work out what a cake costs and what to charge.

video.title: How to Make a Vanilla Sponge Cake Recipe

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add the cost of the box, board, and decorations.
Add your time: how many hours did you spend?
A decorated cake costs more than a plain one.
Compare with other bakers near you.
days.task: Cost a celebration cake and set its price.
days.challenge: Cost a box of 12 cupcakes the same way.

quiz.q: What costs go into a cake price?
options: Ingredients, box, board, decorations, and your time
quiz.explain: A fair price covers ingredients, packaging, decorations, and your time.

quiz.q: Why do decorated cakes cost more?
quiz.explain: Decorating is skilled work that takes hours.

options: So your price is fair for your area
quiz.explain: Local prices tell you what customers expect to pay.

days.title: Cake Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest cake problems.

video.title: Vanilla Cupcake Recipe

steps: Cake sank? The oven door was opened too early, or it was under-baked.
Cake is dry? It was over-baked, or it needed more liquid.
Frosting is too soft? The butter was too warm, or it needs more sugar.
Cake stuck to the tin? The tin was not lined or greased.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one cake problem you have had.
days.challenge: Bake a cake and write down what went right and wrong.

options: The oven door was opened too early or it was under-baked
quiz.explain: Opening the door early or under-baking makes a cake fall.
Too long in the oven dries a cake out.
Warm butter makes soft, runny frosting. Chill it to firm it up.

days.goal: Bake and decorate a two-tier cake.

video.title: How to Pipe a Cupcake

steps: Bake two tiers: a big bottom and a smaller top.

days.task: Bake a two-tier cake.
days.challenge: Cost it and work out what you would charge a customer.

quiz.q: Why use dowels in a two-tier cake?
options: They hold the top tier up
quiz.explain: Dowels stop the top tier sinking into the bottom.

quiz.q: What order do you frost tiers in?
options: Frost each tier on its own, then stack

options: Photos show your skill to future customers
quiz.explain: Photos of a two-tier cake prove you can do big cakes.

steps: Use a strong box that fits the cake board.
Put the cake on a board that is bigger than the cake.

days.task: Pack a cake in a box as if for delivery.

quiz.q: Why must the board be bigger than the cake?
options: So you can lift the cake without touching it

quiz.q: Why keep a cake flat in the car?

steps: Ask the date, the number of people, and the flavour.

days.task: Practise taking an order from a friend.
days.challenge: Write an order form you can use for real customers.

options: So you do not use an ingredient that could harm someone
quiz.explain: Allergies can be serious. Always ask and write the answer down.

options: Money paid in advance to book the cake
quiz.explain: A deposit books the order and covers your costs if the customer cancels.

days.goal: Plan cakes for Christmas and birthdays.

options: The day before, so it is fresh
quiz.explain: Decorating the day before keeps the cake fresh.

quiz.q: What makes a good birthday cake?

quiz.explain: A birthday cake should suit the person it is for.

days.goal: Choose and perfect one cake you can make brilliantly.

capstone.title: The Celebration Cake: Baked, Frosted and Decorated
capstone.brief: Bake, frost, and decorate a full celebration cake for a birthday or event: two layers, smooth buttercream, piped decoration, and a simple topper. Cost the cake, pack it safely, and deliver or serve it on time.
checks: Cake planned with a shopping list and costs
Sponge layers baked soft and even
Crumb coat done and chilled before the final coat
Final coat smooth, piping neat and even
Feedback collected from at least one person who tasted it
